server.description: Read, send, file and search email in any IMAP or Microsoft 365 mailbox, and check it arrived.
server.title: Mailbox MCP

com.mailbox-mcp.authentication: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE. Mailbox credentials are envelope-encrypted and are never held by the client.
com.mailbox-mcp.summary: Mailbox MCP connects an assistant to a real mailbox over IMAP and SMTP, so it can read, write, file and search mail the way the owner would. It works with any IMAP host, with Microsoft 365 over OAuth, and with Gmail using an app password. The mailbox has to look untouched afterwards in Outlook or webmail, and that rule decides the implementation: reading never marks a message as read, a send files exactly one copy in Sent, a delete moves to Trash rather than destroying anything, a draft is saved where another client can open and edit it, a move keeps flags and the internal date, and folders resolve by their special-use flag instead of by name. It also answers the question that comes after a send. check_bounces parses the delivery report and says whether an address failed permanently or is still being retried, and check_receipts reports whether a message was opened, including when the honest answer is that nothing came back.
worksWith: Any IMAP and SMTP mail host
Microsoft 365 and Exchange Online, over OAuth
Gmail and Google Workspace, with an app password

server.name: com.mailbox-mcp/mailbox-mcp
server.description: Read, send, file and search email in any Gmail, Microsoft 365 or IMAP mailbox, plus its calendar.
server.title: Mailbox MCP

com.mailbox-mcp.authentication: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE. Mailbox credentials are envelope-encrypted and are never held by the client.
com.mailbox-mcp.summary: Mailbox MCP connects an assistant to a real mailbox over IMAP and SMTP, so it can read, write, file and search mail the way the owner would. The mailbox has to look untouched afterwards in Outlook or webmail, and that rule decides the implementation: reading never marks a message as read, a send files exactly one copy in Sent, a delete moves to Trash rather than destroying anything, a draft is saved where another client can open and edit it, a move keeps flags and the internal date, and folders resolve by their special-use flag instead of by name. The same rule lets it archive and report spam: both are roles rather than folder names, each provider puts them somewhere different, and Gmail has no archive folder at all, so archiving there drops the inbox label instead. It reads attachments too: a PDF, a Word document or a spreadsheet as text, a photo as a picture. It also answers the question that comes after a send. check_bounces parses the delivery report and says whether an address failed permanently or is still being retried, and check_receipts reports whether a message was opened, including when the honest answer is that nothing came back. Where the owner has also connected a diary, and that is a separate step from connecting the mailbox, the same connector gains calendar tools: reading and searching events, checking when a group is free, booking and moving your own time, inviting people and cancelling properly, answering an invitation or proposing another time, and reading or setting the out-of-office reply. A mailbox with no diary is handed none of them rather than tools that would refuse, so the tool count varies by mailbox.
com.mailbox-mcp.toolsNote: This list is the mail surface, which every connected mailbox gets. The calendar tools are deliberately absent from it: they are registered only on a mailbox whose owner has connected a diary, which is a separate step, so a client listing tools against a mailbox without one would not see them and the listing would be a promise the server had not kept. What a diary adds is described in the summary.

Microsoft 365 and Exchange Online, over OAuth
Gmail and Google Workspace, with an app password
Microsoft 365 and Google calendars, over OAuth

com.mailbox-mcp.authentication: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE. Mailbox credentials are envelope-encrypted and are never held by the client.
com.mailbox-mcp.summary: Mailbox MCP connects an assistant to a real mailbox over IMAP and SMTP, so it can read, write, file and search mail the way the owner would. The mailbox has to look untouched afterwards in Outlook or webmail, and that rule decides the implementation: reading never marks a message as read, a send files exactly one copy in Sent, a delete moves to Trash rather than destroying anything, a draft is saved where another client can open and edit it, a move keeps flags and the internal date, and folders resolve by their special-use flag instead of by name. The same rule lets it archive and report spam: both are roles rather than folder names, each provider puts them somewhere different, and Gmail has no archive folder at all, so archiving there drops the inbox label instead. It reads attachments too: a PDF, a Word document or a spreadsheet as text, a photo as a picture. It also answers the question that comes after a send. check_bounces parses the delivery report and says whether an address failed permanently or is still being retried, and check_receipts reports whether a message was opened, including when the honest answer is that nothing came back. Where the owner has also connected a diary, and that is a separate step from connecting the mailbox, the same connector gains calendar tools: reading and searching events, checking when a group is free, booking and moving your own time, inviting people and cancelling properly, answering an invitation or proposing another time, and reading or setting the out-of-office reply. A mailbox with no diary is handed none of them rather than tools that would refuse, so the tool count varies by mailbox.
com.mailbox-mcp.toolsNote: This list is the mail surface, which every connected mailbox gets. The calendar tools are deliberately absent from it: they are registered only on a mailbox whose owner has connected a diary, which is a separate step, so a client listing tools against a mailbox without one would not see them and the listing would be a promise the server had not kept. What a diary adds is described in the summary.
